newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end lower on institutional sales.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end lower on institutional sales.

text.p: Singapore shares fell sharply late on Wednesday on institutional selling of blue chips, but retail demand protected small and over-the-counter issues.
Dealers said the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was assaulted by liquidation of several big counters like Cycle & Carriage, UOB Bank and Fraser & Neave.
"The market has been very thin. In such conditions it's easy to move sharply up or down," a U.S. brokerage dealer said.
The STII slipped to a two-year intraday low of 2,026.63 before recovering to close at 2,034.80, down 12.76 points. The last time the index struck 2,026 was in April, 1995.
Volume was relatively thin at 150 million shares.
Dealers said they expect further foreign fund selling and reallocation of assets to drag the index down to 2,000 points.
Initial momentum on the back of Wall Street's rally faded over the thin session.
Cycle & Carriage fell Singapore 70 cents to S$14.80, and Creative Technology eased S$1.00 to S$19.60.
Among actives, SM Summit ended up three cents at S$1.05 on speculation about a rights or bonus issue and Singapore Telecom rebounded from new S$2.59 lows to end two cents off at $2.62.
